title:
VECTORS,
(WRITING AND REPRESENTING VECTORS)
objective: LO: I can write vectors using column notation and represent them on a grid.

content.text: A vector describes a movement with both magnitude (size) and direction. We write column vectors as (x, y) where x is the horizontal movement and y is the vertical movement.
Convention: Positive x means right, negative x means left. Positive y means up, negative y means down. Vectors are equal if they have the same magnitude and direction.

examples.expr: (3, 2) and (3, 2) drawn at different points are equal

examples.desc: x is horizontal (first), y is vertical (second)

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: A column vector gives horizontal then vertical displacement. Equal vectors have the same column vector regardless of starting point.
key_idea.caption: Right and up are positive; left and down are negative

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – writing a column vector
modelled_examples.question: Write the vector that moves from A(1, 3) to B(4, 7) as a column vector.
modelled_examples.explanation: Subtract the start coordinates from the end coordinates.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – negative components
modelled_examples.question: Write the vector from P(5, 6) to Q(2, 1).
modelled_examples.explanation: Negative values show movement left or down.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – drawing a vector on a grid
modelled_examples.question: Draw the vector (4, -2) starting from point (1, 5).
modelled_examples.explanation: Plot the start, apply the vector, mark the end with an arrow.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – identifying equal vectors
modelled_examples.question: Are (2, 3) from A(0, 0) and (2, 3) from B(4, 1) equal vectors?
steps: Same magnitude and direction, so they are equal
modelled_examples.explanation: Position does not matter; only magnitude and direction define a vector.

practice.heading: Writing column vectors
practice.instruction: Write each movement as a column vector.

practice.heading: From coordinates
practice.instruction: Find the column vector from the first point to the second.

practice.heading: Drawing vectors
practice.instruction: Starting from the given point, state the end point after applying the vector.

questions.expression: A to B is (4, 5). B to C is (1, -3). Find A to C.
P to Q is (-2, 6). What is Q to P?
Are (4, -1) and (-4, 1) equal, opposite, or neither?

items.statement: Two vectors with the same column vector are equal regardless of position

problems.text: A drone starts at position (2, 3) on a grid. It follows three vectors in sequence: (4, 1), then (-2, 5), then (1, -3). What is the drone’s final position? Write a single vector that would take the drone directly from start to finish.
Points A(1, 2), B(4, 6), C(7, 10) lie on a grid. Write the vectors AB and BC as column vectors. What do you notice? Explain why A, B, and C must be collinear (lie on the same straight line).
